PlussTilsView In-House Window Runtime¶

Runtime contract¶

PlussWebView parses HTML, lays out the document, paints a software-rendered pixel canvas, and presents that canvas in an operating-system window. It does not delegate HTML rendering or scrolling to WebKit.

Select it through HtmlWindowOptions::backend_preference:

pluss::view::HtmlWindowOptions options;
options.backend_preference = pluss::view::BackendPreference::PlussWebViewOnly;
pluss::view::show_html_window(html, options);

Scrolling behavior¶

The in-house viewer exposes independent two-axis scroll regions for the document and for every rendered table.

  • A trackpad scroll preserves the platform’s precise pixel delta.

  • A wheel notch advances by a stable 40-pixel line step.

  • The region under the pointer receives the input.

  • When a nested table reaches an edge, unused movement continues into the document.

  • Shift plus a vertical wheel scrolls horizontally.

  • Horizontal and vertical scrollbar tracks support page clicks.

  • Scrollbar thumbs support direct dragging.

  • Dragging table or document content pans it on both axes.

  • Table positions remain independent and survive temporary removal from the visible layout.

  • Resizing clamps every offset to the new content boundary.

Keyboard commands are Up, Down, Left, Right, Page Up, Page Down, Home, and End. Keyboard input targets the region beneath the most recent pointer position and otherwise targets the document.

Runtime components¶

  • Scene stores renderer commands.

  • PixelCanvas owns the RGBA frame.

  • SoftwareRenderer rasterizes scenes with nested clipping.

  • ViewerRuntime owns canvas configuration and frame submission.

  • HtmlScrollModel owns floating-point offsets, nested routing, edge propagation, keyboard navigation, and pointer dragging.

  • IWindowShell carries resize, pointer, text, and shortcut events.

  • CocoaWindowShell is the current native shell implementation.

HtmlRenderStats is the contract between layout and input. It publishes document overflow, table scroll regions, and track/thumb rectangles after every layout. HtmlScrollModel::update_metrics() consumes those values and clamps state before the next frame.

Validation¶

Build and run the focused regression suite:

cmake --build build_cpp_env --target plussview_html_scroll_tests
ctest --test-dir build_cpp_env -R plussview_html_scroll_tests --output-on-failure

The suite covers horizontal and vertical document overflow, nested edge propagation, multiple independent tables, anonymous table identity, precise and notched input, Shift-wheel mapping, track clicks, thumb dragging, content dragging, keyboard navigation, resize clamping, and visible frame changes.

The plusstils_view_inhouse_scroll_showcase target opens the real PlussWebViewOnly Cocoa path with wide and tall document content plus two independently scrollable tables.

Remaining platform gaps¶

  1. Linux and Windows still need in-house native shell adapters.

  2. Text shaping and font fallback do not yet cover the full Unicode surface.

  3. The software renderer is CPU-based; there is no GPU compositor.
